_source: Lucid Trading published rules, compiled 2026-08-22. Marketing page supplied by Jakob contained NO numeric rules; every figure below came from secondary rule aggregators plus the Lucid help centre index. See _verification.

_verification.caveat: These are SECONDARY sources. support.lucidtrading.com returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so the primary help-centre articles were NOT read directly. Before funding a real account, confirm every number against the Lucid portal. The instrument-freshness discipline added 2026-08-21 applies here: this is a dated external rule set and it must be re-verified, not trusted because it was once written down.

universal.drawdown_trails: highest CLOSING balance only - intraday highs and lows never move it and never breach it
universal.drawdown_locks_at: initial_balance + 100, once the account CLOSES above the Initial Trail Balance
universal.news_trading: allowed on Pro, Flex and Direct

LucidPro.dll_type: soft - locks the session, does not fail the account
LucidPro.scaling: once funded, DLL graduates to LucidScale = 60% of highest end-of-day profit; ratchets up only

LucidFlex.scaling: contract size scales up AND down with account profit once funded
LucidFlex.payout_gate: five separate trading days each clearing the minimum daily profit for the size

LucidDirect.dll_type: soft, graduates to LucidScale = 60% of highest end-of-day profit once above Initial Trail Balance

_conflicts_not_resolved: LucidDirect 100k/150k max_loss: one source says 3000/4500 (same as Pro), another says 3500/5000. The LARGER figure is used above only where a source stated it explicitly for Direct; treat Direct sizing as the least certain in this file.

LucidPro eval consistency: one source says 40% applies to the evaluation, another says the eval has none and 40% is funded-only. This file assumes funded-only, which is the LESS permissive reading for eval sizing and the MORE dangerous one if wrong - so eval trades are sized as if 40% applies anyway.
LucidBlack appears discontinued for new traders and is not modelled.
